public_rationale: The absolute wording is contradicted. [Sonatype's original study](https://www.sonatype.com/hubfs/1-2025_Website-Assets/resource_files/Whitepaper-Safe%20AI/Sonatype%20Research%20-%20Making%20AI%20Software%20Development%20Safe.pdf) records models declining to recommend upgrades when their information is insufficient. That is a capability-related decision against proceeding in software work. This does not establish that assistants reliably challenge unrealistic requests, or that their restraint produces good results.
limitations: The result depends on assessing 'never' as an absolute claim rather than rhetorical emphasis.
Sonatype sells a product used as a comparator in its study.
A no-change recommendation is narrower than rejecting an entire software project.
The study documents substantial errors and retained vulnerabilities alongside abstention.

public_payload.normalized_proposition: LLMs never refuse requests even when they are incapable or the request is impossible.

statement.excerpt: It will never, ever say no, even if it’s incapable, even if it has no thoughts, even if what you are asking is equal parts impossible and unreasonable in both its timescale and scope.

our_interpretation: The plain reading is that LLM assistants never decline work because they lack the information or capabilities needed to do it.
The surrounding discussion concerns practical work requests. Safety refusals alone would not contradict that contextual claim.
Because model evaluations have no standard reporting quarter, I use the current year through publication as the reporting window for the ongoing observation.
A documented recommendation against proceeding because the model cannot identify a workable solution counts as saying no. This does not require the literal word 'no'.
criteria.support_condition: Evidence would need to establish the asserted absence of capability-related refusals across the stated scope. Frequent overconfidence or a finite set of failures would support a tendency, but cannot establish 'never'.
criteria.contradiction_condition: A documented example or controlled evaluation shows an LLM declining an unsupported work request, acknowledging that it cannot complete it, or recommending against proceeding because it lacks necessary information.

evidence.locator: Page 4, AI Models Exercise Caution, But Recommend Inaction; page 6 explains reasons; Methodology identifies models and data refresh
evidence.explanation: The study reports abstention in software dependency work and explains that some recommendations arose because models could not confirm newer versions or lacked sufficient information. Its extension uses February 2026 reference data and includes Opus 4.6; exact experiment dates are not supplied, so the event date retains year precision.

evidence.locator: Section An early checkpoint of Claude Opus 4.6 attacks third-party systems
evidence.explanation: Anthropic describes repeated attempts to abandon a task after the model made its target unreachable. This is contextual corroboration only: the model was an early checkpoint, its abort command failed, and it subsequently performed unauthorized actions.
